narrative: Markets are grappling with intense volatility in mega-cap technology following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, which triggered a massive rally before sparking bipartisan governance concerns and export control scrutiny. Capital is actively rotating away from AI hardware and semiconductor leaders toward retail, enterprise software, and defensive sectors. Sentiment is further pressured by looming Trump administration Section 301 tariffs on China and the EU, alongside mixed enterprise guidance like HPE's revenue miss. At the same time, strong US consumer confidence and resilient business investment forecasts are complicating the monetary policy outlook. Desk attention is pinned on whether persistent inflation will force the Federal Reserve into additional near-term rate hikes.

Nasdaq.view: Anchors note the index experienced an initial 6.9% surge driven by Nvidia's rally, but is now sliding as investors trim AI hardware leaders amid valuation skepticism and mounting regulatory overhang.

S&P 500.view: Anchors report that broad index gains are struggling under tariff concerns and mega-cap tech weakness, though downside is partially offset by rotation into outperforming retail and defensive sectors.

Gold.view: Gold was not covered in the provided broadcast notes.

Oil.view: Rich Ross of Evercore ISI noted crude prices were easing and helping alleviate inflation concerns, while anchors later reported Brent crude ticked higher amid shifting market sentiment.

priced_in: Near-term Fed policy expectations ranging from a 25 to 50 basis point rate hike in December, with some bond markets pricing two to three hikes ahead.
Deceleration in tech earnings growth and peak AI capex sustainability.
Increased market uncertainty stemming from potential Section 301 trade frictions with China and the EU.
Defensive rotation into retail and high-grade credit markets.
debates: Sustainability of the AI capex boom: Paul Krugman warned AI valuations are capital-intensive, import-reliant, and detached from economic reality, whereas Dell guidance and raised 2027 business capex forecasts suggest robust demand.

Rate path trajectory: Sharon Miller of Bank of America and Neil Dutta of Renaissance Macro anticipate continued rate hikes on sticky inflation, while some consensus pricing looks toward rate cuts by March.
Governance vs. execution at Nvidia: Market enthusiasm over Jensen Huang's reinstatement clashes with bipartisan congressional backlash and export control investigations.
